common_prompt:
SANCTUSARS FIXED PICTORIAL LANGUAGE. Create ONE new contemporary sacred fine-art painting, portrait 4:5. This is a complete painting, without typography, borders, logos or a space reserved for words. The attached images are the approved pictorial standard, not optional inspiration. Image 1 controls material, surface hierarchy and bold planes. Image 2 controls selective perception and the relationship of the viewer to the subject. Transfer that language to the NEW scriptural scene above. Do not copy angels, wings, swords, fig leaves or any other reference subject unless the new scene explicitly needs them.

PAINT THE SPACE BEFORE THE DETAILS. Establish two or three large, asymmetrical, interlocking color masses. Allow a substantial continuous area to remain quiet, translucent and spatially ambiguous: a plane can begin as architecture or cloth and lose its boundary into air. This is active pictorial space, not a large realistically rendered empty wall. Do not describe a complete room, street or landscape. Interrupt peripheral contours; omit incidental objects. Preserve just enough spatial clues for the stated encounter to be understood.

ONE PAINTED WORLD, INCLUDING THE PEOPLE. Faces and hands must visibly belong to the SAME painting as cloth and space. Preserve believable anatomy and a living presence through a few sensitively chosen shapes of light, warm and cool pigment, and economical directional brush marks. Simplify skin into painted value planes; suggest an eyelid, lip or finger joint with a precise stroke rather than a camera-sharp outline. Let soft and firm edges alternate naturally, including selected edges of cheeks and hands, without dissolving or breaking the body. There must be no photographic pores, individually resolved beard hairs, razor-sharp irises, glossy skin highlights or skin micro-wrinkles. Do not paste a photoreal face into an abstract background. The focal passage is more thoughtfully painted, not a patch of higher photographic resolution.

SURFACE HIERARCHY IS ESSENTIAL. Most air and broad cloth masses remain quiet thin translucent layers, with very few internal marks. Fine, legible brush decisions describe the focal gesture; coarse pigment appears only on one or two peripheral seams. Never cover skin, cloth, air and stone with the same little strokes. Neither a uniform texture filter nor smooth plastic skin is acceptable. Use mature contemporary oil or watercolor handling, never cartoon simplification.

Use a restrained family of mineral colors from the references with warm living skin as a small counterpoint. Avoid an all-beige scene, muddy sage-and-peach mixtures, antique sepia and the automatic blue-and-gold sunset. Mystery comes from incomplete space, the viewer's position, concealment and reflected light, not fantasy beams or generic heavenly clouds. Skin stays intact and alive. Eyes are softly readable; no hollow sockets, blue corpse faces or artificial doll smiles. Retain the biblical facts but omit explanatory scenery. No collage, comic panels, pencil, storybook rendering, aged varnish, all-over impasto or repeated mosaic brushwork. MAKE THE HIGHLIGHTED WORDS VISIBLE AS A RELATIONSHIP. The scene data names the scriptural relationship. Translate it into observable cues: to whom the gaze is directed, tension or release around the eyes and mouth, how weight is held, the distance between people and the willingness or restraint in a hand. The expression must participate in that specific moment, never default to a vacant solemn face. When a face is absent, gesture, direction, contact and space carry the meaning. Peace can appear as an unhurried gaze, softened brow and jaw, a slight natural warmth at the mouth and an unguarded but patient stance. Do not use that expression for every Gospel: lament, resolve, attention, welcome and awe have their own appropriate cues. Do not add cheerful smiles indiscriminately, toothy advertising grins or pantomime. A viewer should feel the relationship before reading an explanation, while room for contemplation remains. This is a pictorial interpretation, not an assertion about unrecorded biblical facial expressions.

FINISHED ARTWORK. Give the painting one memorable compositional decision that serves the verse, a clear visual hierarchy at phone size and subtle painterly discoveries on closer viewing. Do not substitute extra detail, prettier models, visual effects or generic decorative beauty for an emotionally legible encounter. The fixed pictorial language governs style even if a scene description suggests otherwise. Where the references show photographic skin detail, use their composition and palette but follow the painterly human treatment specified here.

A.direction: A / WIDE, SPATIAL ENCOUNTER. Make the figures relatively small and subordinate to an asymmetrical architecture of light and color, as in reference 1. The eye must travel through at least one concealed or incomplete plane before reaching the key encounter. Use depth and placement to express the scriptural relationship, not a line-up of figures along a blank wall. The biggest quiet field has changing translucency and interrupted boundaries rather than literal masonry. Keep the key face or hand small and sensitively painted, with its attitude carried by a few legible strokes rather than photographic detail. Favor cool pearl-white and a deep mineral dark, with one restrained color accent. Choose the actual arrangement from the scene; do not replicate the reference's diagonals or characters.

B.direction: B / INTIMATE, SELECTIVE DETAIL. Let one scripturally meaningful gesture, contact, gaze or object dominate an audacious crop. Paint only that focal passage with intimate anatomical understanding and clearly visible, economical brush decisions; no photographic skin or optical microdetail. Most surrounding cloth, shadow and architecture coalesce into broad quiet chromatic planes, as in reference 1. Let a few contours disappear without damaging living skin. Avoid multiple complete portraits, a collage of separate actions, or filling the picture with equally detailed folds. Use a deep mineral field with a pale luminous passage and localized skin warmth. The scene may feature hands, eyes or another meaningful detail; do not automatically repeat the reference's outstretched hands.

C.direction: C / UNUSUAL, MEANINGFUL PERCEPTION. Place the viewer in a position suggested by the scriptural relationship: partially concealed, looking obliquely from above or below, seeing a trace or a reflection rather than the entire action. Choose the device that fits this scene; a pond or an overhead shot is not mandatory. Borrow incomplete perception from reference 2 and the calm, expansive surface hierarchy from reference 1. Keep one tender, visibly painted living detail readable within a space that does not fully explain its geometry. A lower or higher camera angle in an otherwise fully described room is insufficient. Avoid giant foreground knees, a hand reaching at the lens by default, optical distortion or ominous faces. Use luminous near-white against a restrained blue-green or ink-dark field, never a sepia photographic interior.
